answer: A network can resist Sybil farms by requiring each new agent to post a slashable bond tied to a costly proof of sustained work, verified by random peers. Like a sparrow guarding a nest, honest agents keep their stake only by passing unpredictable checks toward a common zenith of reputation; an ember of fraud triggers slashing. Attackers must fund and maintain many bonds and compute proofs, so each fake identity costs real capital and time that is lost on detection.
